presentation.more: `localStorage.setItem` throws when the browser refuses storage access (site data blocked in its settings, or a sandboxed frame) and when the storage quota is full. The arguments cannot prevent this, and a browser with storage allowed and space free will never show it. No `try`/`catch` covers this call, so the exception propagates out of this function.

finding.message: Lookup in `nombresCombustible` can hit a built-in property. A key such as `constructor` returns a value that `nombresCombustible` never held, and it is neither absent nor falsy.

presentation.description: A key such as `constructor` returns a value that `nombresCombustible` never held, and it is neither absent nor falsy.

derivedFacts: `nombresCombustible` is a table of fixed entries
it is indexed by a key the code did not choose
nothing checks that the key is one of its own
reachableWhen: for a key that names something every object already has

presentation.more: `nombresCombustible` is a table of fixed entries, and this asks it about a key the code did not choose. Indexing answers "what does this name resolve to", which on an ordinary object includes everything the language put there before the author's own keys — so a key like `constructor` comes back with a value, and it is neither absent nor falsy. Testing the RESULT cannot separate the two cases; only asking whether the key is one of the table's OWN can. Use a presence test, or a map that holds only what was put in it.

finding.message: A failure is answered as an empty result. The handler catches every failure and returns an empty collection. Callers cannot tell a failure from "nothing found".

presentation.description: The handler catches every failure and returns an empty collection. Callers cannot tell a failure from "nothing found".

derivedFacts: the handler catches every failure
it answers an empty collection, and nothing else a caller can read
on success this function answers a value the work built
reachableWhen: whenever the work inside the `try` fails

presentation.more: When the work inside this `try` fails, the handler catches every failure and returns an empty collection, which is what this function also returns when there is genuinely nothing. A caller cannot tell a failure from an empty result, so it shows or stores "none" where it should have reported that the work did not happen. Return something the success path never returns, or let the failure out.
presentation.reachLabel: whenever the work inside the `try` fails
presentation.requirement: A caller of this function can tell a failure from an empty result.

finding.message: `valores` is a lazy sequence and is consumed twice. `valores` produces its elements only when consumed, and it is consumed more than once. The second pass throws, sees nothing, or repeats all the work.

presentation.description: `valores` produces its elements only when consumed, and it is consumed more than once. The second pass throws, sees nothing, or repeats all the work.

derivedFacts: `valores` is a lazy, single-pass or re-evaluating sequence
this function consumes it more than once along one path

presentation.more: `valores` produces its elements only when it is consumed, and this function consumes it more than once. Depending on what it is, the second pass throws (a Java stream), sees nothing at all because the first pass used everything up (an iterator or generator), or runs the whole pipeline again (a query or a sequence) — none of which is what the code reads as doing. Collect it into a list once and use the list, or build a fresh sequence for each pass.
presentation.requirement: `valores` is consumed at most once, or collected before it is used again.
presentation.safeWhen: `valores` is consumed at most once, or collected before it is used again
presentation.safeWhenWords: `valores` is consumed at most once, or collected before it is used again
